job.title: Investor Relations Coordinator
job.description:
Job Brief

This is the ideal entry role into investor relations for someone with strong coordination, executive support or corporate affairs experience. It is a genuine coordination role at the centre of a busy IR function. You will work closely with the General Manager and Senior Manager of Investor Relations, providing the structure and discipline that keeps calendars, materials, disclosure and stakeholder coordination running properly.
 
About Our Client

Our client is a growing, privately backed business with a lean executive team, currently building out its investor relations function as it scales. 
 
Responsibilities
  • Coordinate the IR calendar, including results, trading updates, AGMs, investor days, roadshows, conferences and one on one meetings
  • Coordinate travel and logistics for interstate investor meetings and roadshows
  • Support production, version control and sign off tracking for investor materials, ASX announcements, presentations and annual reporting content
  • Work with Legal and Company Secretariat on the disclosure workflow, including tracking drafts, managing comments, running sign off checklists and coordinating ASX release logistics
  • Coordinate investor website updates, webcast logistics and digital investor materials with Communications, Legal, IT and external providers
  • Manage the day to day operation of the investor CRM, including logging interactions, maintaining contact records and preparing reports for management and the Board
  • Coordinate shareholder register monitoring, share registry requests, targeting lists, proxy adviser tracking and analyst coverage records
  • Coordinate with capital markets advisers, legal counsel, PR advisers and share registry providers on process, timelines and deliverables
 
Requirements
  • 5+ years in coordination, program management, executive support, corporate affairs, capital markets operations or corporate access
  • Experience ideally gained in a listed company, transaction, professional services or investment banking environment
  • Demonstrated ability to coordinate multi stakeholder processes involving senior executives, external advisers, legal counsel, governance stakeholders or investors
  • Strong written communication and document discipline, with the ability to produce executive ready materials and maintain clear version control
  • Strong organisational skills across calendar management, travel, events, workflow tracking, meeting preparation and follow up
  • Familiarity with IR, governance or capital markets tools such as Microsoft 365, IR CRM platforms, share registry systems, market data services or virtual data rooms
  • High discretion and sound judgement, with experience handling confidential or market sensitive information
    Comfort working through unfamiliar tasks where there is no set template
  • Exposure to technology, infrastructure, energy, AI, data centres or other complex project based sectors is a plus
What's on Offer

Direct exposure to how investor messaging, disclosure and market engagement come together, working closely with the General Manager and Senior Manager of Investor Relations, with room to grow as the function scales.
Apply via link or contact Carolina for a confidential discussion.

job.title: Finance Systems & Automation Analyst

Permanent, full time

The finance team is building out its systems, data and processes to support that growth, with a strong focus on automation and practical use of AI. This role sits in a small team reporting to the Finance Systems & Automation Lead.

  • Find faster ways to get data out of NetSuite and into reporting the business can act on

  • CA or CPA qualified
  • 2 to 5 years of experience in finance systems, business analysis, finance transformation or a related role
  • Hands on experience supporting or administering NetSuite, including troubleshooting, configuration changes, user access and permissions, saved searches and reports
  • Solid knowledge of core finance processes such as procure to pay, order to cash and record to report, and how they run within the system
  • Experience gathering requirements, mapping processes, testing and implementing system changes

job.title: Interim CFO
job.description:

There is a clear growth trajectory to significantly grow in size through organic growth and targeted M&A. It is entrepreneurial, fast-paced, and driven with a leadership team focused on long-term success.

The role requires a hands-on leader - someone who can operate at both strategic and tactical levels. Key areas include:
  • Drive commercial and FP&A requirements
  • Maintain high levels of financial governance, risk and compliance
  • Guide and develop a high-performing, future-ready finance team. Where possible, embed AI, automation, and analytics to drive insights and efficiencies

  • Forge strong stakeholder relationships with banks, investors, auditors, and external partners

job.title: Senior Brand Manager
job.description:
The Company:
We are one of Australia's most established consumer healthcare businesses, the company behind some of the most trusted names in the country's medicine cabinets. With global parent backing, they work with the pace and autonomy of a lean local business. The portfolio leads its categories, with deep consumer trust, strong healthcare-professional endorsement and real scale across pharmacy and grocery. After years of steady growth, they're at an inflection point. Consumer habits in their categories are shifting fast, and changing how to engage a younger, health-conscious consumer. Our marketing team is flatter and low-ego, and it's building new skills in content, social and the smart use of AI.

The Role:
This Senior Brand Manager role owns the flagship brand portfolio, a $130m+ business and the engine of the company. You'll report to a senior Marketing Manager and have full commercial accountability for a market leader that new challenger brands are taking on. The brief is to defend and grow its position, reconnect it with the next generation of consumers and lead a significant innovation pipeline.

Key responsibilities include:
  • Own the P&L and a sizeable A&P budget, including forecasting, pricing, S&OP and monthly reconciliation to plan
  • Develop and deliver the annual brand plan while building on the three-year strategy, and get cross-functional teams aligned behind it
  • Shape the future portfolio: brand architecture, sub-ranges, SKU rationalisation and an innovation pipeline of 12+ launches
  • Lead integrated consumer and trade communications, including digital, social and PR, with external agency partners
  • Partner with senior Sales and National Account Managers across pharmacy, grocery and e-commerce, including range reviews
  • Coach and develop the Assistant Brand Managers in the brand team, and support healthcare-professional engagement
What You'll Bring:
  • Seasoned Senior Brand Manager experience, ideally in FMCG within health, wellness or pharmacy, with a strong track record of owning a brand end to end
  • Full A-to-Z brand management skills, where brand planning, forecasting, pricing, NPD, rationalisation and deletions are second nature
  • Commercial gravitas: the credibility to partner with senior Sales and drive the brand agenda like a commercial partner, not just a marketer
  • Experience across pharmacy (especially Chemist Warehouse), grocery (Coles/Woolworths) and e-commerce (Amazon)
  • A balance of art and science: as comfortable digging into data (IQVIA, IRI or similar) as judging a creative idea
  • People leadership experience, having managed or coached at least one team member, plus a bias for action and comfort with a high degree of autonomy
Why Join?
This is a rare chance to take real ownership of one of Australia's most trusted healthcare brands. You'll have real commercial stakes, a significant A&P budget and the mandate to shape where the brand goes next, without the layers of global approval that slow bigger businesses down. You'll work directly with sales on pricing and portfolio decisions. Reporting to a Senior Marketing Manager with more than 20 years' experience across pharmaceutical, healthcare and consumer brands. An open-door and empathetic style, sets high expectations and puts a lot into coaching the team. With a clear path to Marketing Manager, this is a smart career move for a senior brand leader.

How to Apply:
To be considered, click 'apply' and submit your application. Questions can be directed to Ben Carnegie by writing to benc@axr.com.au

job.title: Global RGM Manager
job.description:

It's an immediate start, running through to approximately end of April 2027. You'll report directly to the Global RGM Director, joining at a genuinely early point as Revenue Growth Management is stood up as a proper standalone global function — moving well beyond the pricing-only remit it's historically had in some markets.

The role is a genuine blend: you'll act as commercial business partner to regional teams across the globe on a prioritised project basis, while also playing a central role in building the frameworks, playbooks, and technology foundations the wider function will run on. There's real autonomy here to shape how things get done, not just execute someone else's playbook.

job.title: Financial Controller
job.description:
Across dozens of countries, this business ended up with a different reconciliation standard in every location — inconsistent, patchy, risky. This role exists to make Record-to-Report one global process, not fifty local ones.

This is a newly created Global R2R Controller role — genuinely flexible on WFH, with a circa $250K package (inclusive of super) plus an STI. You'll join a large, global professional services organisation with a significant offshore shared services footprint, reporting to the Group Financial Controller. Record-to-Report here has never had a single global owner, and this is that role: first-generation standards and a first-generation control framework, built from scratch across a genuinely international, multi-currency footprint.

What the role looks like
  • Design and own the global R2R standards — month-end close model and calendar, journal policies, balance sheet reconciliation standards, and intercompany accounting — across a multi-country, multi-currency footprint.
  • Build and own the R2R control framework, including key controls, evidence and audit trail requirements, testing cadence, and segregation of duties, as the single source of truth for how R2R is done globally.
  • Provide second-line governance and oversight of R2R execution across an offshore shared services centre and regional finance teams — monitor compliance, approve exceptions, and act as final decision-maker on standards.
  • Own the monthly close model end to end — calendar, sign-offs, workflows — and drive continuous improvement in close speed and predictability without adding risk.
  • Lead the global R2R improvement agenda, including where automation genuinely reduces manual effort, and act as gatekeeper for process and system changes touching close or reconciliations.
  • Be the primary point of contact for internal audit on R2R findings, driving root-cause fixes rather than one-off remediation.
What you'll need
  • A senior finance leader with genuine end-to-end Record-to-Report experience — not just the reporting half or the reconciliation half, but both, and how they connect.
  • Strong technical controllership and big 4 audit background with ASX experience, and with a real understanding of risk, control effectiveness, and balance sheet integrity.
  • Experience operating in a global shared services model — you know how to influence outcomes through people who don't report to you.
  • Background in a large, complex, international business with multi-currency exposure; experience in engineering services, or project-based services environments is well regarded.
  • Comfortable owning an unstructured, self-directed mandate — you'll be defining the job as you go, not following a fixed monthly checklist.
  • Hands-on enough to open a reconciliation and know immediately whether it's right, even though you won't be the one doing them day to day.
What makes this worth your time
  • A genuine blank-canvas mandate — refresh and own the global R2R standards from the ground up rather than inherit someone else's framework.
  • Broad influence across a genuinely global finance function, with 1 direct report and no large team overhead to manage.
  • Flexible WFH, with no mandated in-office days.
  • Immediate start available.
This process will move fast — so if this is the kind of mandate you've been looking for, apply now or reach out to Dave Goldbach for a confidential conversation.

  • Finance runs through a mix of in-country teams and an offshore shared services centre, so the same process gets done quite differently depending on where you look. Your job is to assess, improve & standardise.
  • You will report to the GM Finance, with real backing from senior finance leadership.
What the Role Involves
  • Refreshing the global R2R standards first up. Month end close, journals, balance sheet reconciliations and intercompany transactions.
  • You'll help set the global standard and then make sure it actually sticks.
  • Oversight of the balance sheet rather than doing the recs yourself, including targeted reviews of high risk areas and getting aged items cleared.
  • Owning the R2R control framework, segregation of duties included.
  • Any internal audit findings that touch R2R come to you to resolve properly, root cause and all.
  • Driving more automation across journals and intercompany, and looking at where AI can take out manual work (alongside a transformation lead already in place).
  • One direct report, but a big network of finance teams relying on your standards who don't report to you.
Ideal Background / Experience
  • Established senior finance leader, not after a first step up.
  • Audit background, then controllership in a large listed business.
  • Genuine end to end R2R experience, from how a transaction is recorded right through to what gets reported.
  • You've worked with an offshore shared services or outsourced model and know how to get the best out of one.
  • International and multi-currency exposure is important here.
  • Oracle, BlackLine and EPM or similar, and happy to get into the detail in Excel when needed.
  • Comfortable with ambiguity. There's no set weekly list of deliverables, so you'll need to be someone who works out what matters and gets on with it.
  • A services or project-based background is a plus but not essential.
What's on Offer
  • circa $250k including super, plus STI.
  • Sydney based.
  • Flexibility, no mandated office days. It's a global role so some non-standard hours come with it.
  • Good timing to join, with year end done and half year still a way off.

job.title: Senior Treasury Manager - Project & Asset Finance
job.description:
Overview

 We're working with a business at the centre of the digital and energy infrastructure build-out, operating in a sector absorbing very large amounts of capital right now. The financing is constant, and the assets are significant. What the business needs is someone to run the treasury function that sits behind those facilities properly, and to build the processes that will hold as it scales.

It's a hands-on operational treasury role with genuine technical depth, and the person who takes it will end up knowing the underlying business model better than almost anyone.

The role
  • Manage the existing facilities day to day. Key terms, rate sets, interest accruals, fee amortisation, and the monthly compliance cycle including covenant certificates and lender reporting
  • Run the cash waterfall. Facility payments, transfers to and from liquidity accounts, controlled account reconciliations and minimum balance requirements
  • Own weekly funding and cash forecasting across project-level and corporate requirements, with the FX that goes alongside it
  • Manage the hedging operations. Confirmations, settlements, ISDA documentation, valuations and hedge accounting support, working with the GM Treasury on strategy
  • Maintain and update the covenant model, and produce the monthly reporting that lenders, equity investors and SPV arrangements require
  • Bank guarantees, counterparty credit reporting, KYC and treasury controls
  • Lead the treasury management system implementation, automated bank feeds and straight-through processing
What we're looking for
  • Five or more years across corporate treasury, project finance operations or structured finance
  • Project or asset-level financing experience, not just group facilities. This is the requirement that matters most. If you've managed a real facility with real CPs, a real waterfall and real covenant tests, you'll recognise this role immediately
  • Comfort with the financial model. You'll be updating covenant models and reconciling them to reporting, so this needs to be a strength rather than something you delegate
  • Working knowledge of FX and derivatives, ISDAs, confirmations, settlements and hedge accounting support
  • Strong systems capability across ERP, banking platforms and treasury systems, and an interest in automating what's currently manual
  • Control discipline and attention to detail. A lot of what you produce goes to lenders, so accuracy is the baseline
Worth being direct about one thing. This is an operational treasury role rather than a transaction one. If your background is entirely on the bank side and what you want is deal execution, this probably isn't the right fit.

Why apply
  • A business growing quickly in a sector with global relevance and very few precedents
  • Real ownership. You'd be building the treasury function rather than maintaining someone else's
  • Founder-led, accessible leadership, and decisions that get made in days rather than quarters
For a confidential conversation, apply via the link or reach out to Kunal Gupta directly at kunalg@axr.com.au.
